items.title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side.

Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models.

## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` / `glm5next`) is now supported in vLLM, but its native sparse MLA / KeyPool attention path is not implemented for the CPU backend.

This is different from #54018 / #54029.

Those address the older `glm_moe_dsa` path and provide a way to disable sparse attention and fall back to dense MLA on CPU.

For GLM-5.3-Flash, I would like to request **native CPU execution of its sparse MLA + KeyPool/KeyPoolIndexer path**, preserving the model's sparse-attention behavior rather than converting it to dense MLA.

## Current state on `main`

The generic CPU attention selector still rejects sparse attention:

```python
if attn_selector_config.use_sparse:
    raise NotImplementedError("Sparse Attention is not supported on CPU.")
```

At the same time, CPU support has recently progressed significantly: DeepSeek-V4 now has its own x86/AMX CPU sparse-MLA/indexer implementation, including CPU kernels for the sparse attention/indexing pipeline.

`vllm/platforms/cpu.py` explicitly documents the DeepSeek-V4 CPU kernels under:

```text
csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/
├── flash_mla
├── store_cache
├── compressor
├── paged_mqa_logits
└── topk
```

and configures DeepSeek-V4 separately with its required block size.

This makes GLM5Next support seem like a useful next target rather than requiring CPU sparse attention infrastructure to be created entirely from scratch.

GLM-5.3 uses a different sparse-indexing scheme from DeepSeek-V4.

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) is a hybrid model containing both:

* sparse MLA layers
* KDA (Kimi Delta Attention / gated delta-rule) linear-attention layers

Even if GLM5Next's sparse MLA / KeyPool path is made CPU-compatible, the model still cannot execute end-to-end on CPU without a KDA backend.

I would like to request native CPU support for GLM5Next KDA.

## Current state

The GLM5Next KDA implementation currently lives under the accelerator-specific path:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/kda.py
```

and uses GPU-oriented Flash Linear Attention / Triton operators such as:

```text
chunk_kda_with_fused_gate
fused_recurrent_kda
```

There does not appear to be a corresponding:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/cpu/kda.py
```

or other CPU KDA execution path for GLM5Next on current `main`.

This makes KDA an independent CPU blocker from sparse MLA / KeyPool support.

GLM-5.3-Flash has a large number of KDA layers, so this cannot reasonably be worked around by supporting only the sparse-MLA portion of the model.

## Related CPU infrastructure already exists

The CPU backend already has substantial support for related linear-attention/state-space workloads.

In particular, current CPU platform code contains an accelerated GDN path using:

```text
AMX tiles
or
AVX-512 BF16 / VDPBF16PS
```

and vLLM already has CPU machinery for stateful hybrid models, including:

* recurrent state caches
* convolution state
* chunked prefill
* decode
* hybrid KV/state-cache management

KDA is not identical to GDN, but they are closely related enough that it may be possible to reuse much of this infrastructure.

items.title: [Bug]: NIXL P/D disagg silently corrupts output when hybrid-attention layers share a storage base with different block lengths (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash served via NIXL PD disaggregation (2P×TP8 + 2D×TP8, 2×H200 nodes, RDMA) produces garbled output (nonsensical characters, or empty content/reasoning fields) with no errors or crashes — silent data corruption. The same image serves a single-full-attention model (GLM-5.3) correctly in the same topology. Mooncake, CUDA graphs, and MultiConnector were ruled out.

### Root cause

In `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py`, region registration deduplicates transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshes `block_len/stride/num_blocks` when `is_mla_region` is true.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's `layers.2.attn.compressor.state_cache` (`CircularBufferSpec`, needs block_len=32768) shares its storage base address with `layers.0.attn.swa_cache` (MLA, block_len=19008). It folds into region 0 without updating block_len, so its compressor state is transferred with only 19008 bytes per block and offsets computed from the swa view — truncated and misaligned. `layers.2.attn.indexer.k_cache` hits a second instance of the same base-address conflict.

Diagnostic signature: the affected region simultaneously shows `rgid=-1` (shared), `scratch=True`, and `is_mla=True` — three mutually contradictory attributes. After the fix, `num_regions` grows 12 → 14.

### Fix

Deduplicate by `(base_addr, block_len)`: regions with distinct transfer geometry stay separate; identical-geometry aliases still fold as before. A PR follows.

### Verification

- Cluster (2×8 H200, P/D disagg): before the fix — all-garbled short completions, 200-token generations fully corrupted, Chinese chat returns empty content/reasoning; after the fix — normal English/Chinese output, 0% garble rate over 200-token generations, clean output across 6 concurrent streams.
- Unit tests: new regression test fails on HEAD and passes with the fix; the existing NIXL unit test failure set is byte-identical before/after (no regressions).

items.title: [Bugfix] Forward upstream error message in Anthropic streaming converter (#46028)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #46028.

When the engine fails mid-stream, the OpenAI serving layer emits an `ErrorResponse` payload (`{"error": {...}}`) via `create_streaming_error_response`, followed by `[DONE]`. The Anthropic adapter's `message_stream_converter` validated **every** chunk as a `ChatCompletionStreamResponse`, so the error chunk raised a pydantic `ValidationError`. The outer `except` then re-emitted that as a generic `internal_error` carrying the *pydantic* message — masking the real upstream failure. The reporter hit this serving GLM-5.2, where an engine 500 surfaced only as `2 validation errors for ChatCompletionStreamResponse ... model Field required input_value={'error': {'message': 'Internal Server Error'...}}`.

This PR detects the error payload (new `parse_streaming_error_chunk` helper, mirroring the existing module-level `wrap_data_with_event` helper) and forwards its message as an Anthropic `error` event, reusing the converter's existing `AnthropicStreamEvent(type="error", ...)` shape. Only the failure path changes; valid chunks validate exactly as before.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --search "46028 in:body"` → none.
- `gh pr list --search "message_stream_converter"` → only #45807 (stop_sequence `stop_reason`), unrelated.

items.title: [Bugfix] glm47 parser: tolerate missing opening <arg_value> tag
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

FIX #49248

Under concurrent load, GLM-4.7-family models sporadically skip the opening `<arg_value>` tag when emitting tool calls, producing

```
<tool_call>search<arg_key>query</arg_key>how many vacation days left</arg_value></tool_call>
```

with the argument value fully intact (raw sampled tokens captured via `logprobs: true`; reproduces at `temperature: 0` too, ~5–17% of calls at concurrency 6 on our production trace family, 0 sequentially).

`_ARG_RE`/`_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` in `vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py` require the opening tag, so such calls silently parse to `arguments: "{}"`, which then fails the client's tool schema validation and degrades agent loops (the broken `{}` call gets rendered back into history, so retries tend to fail the same way).

This PR makes the opening `<arg_value>` optional in both regexes. The closing `</arg_value>` still delimits the value, so:
- well-formed output parses exactly as before (the optional group matches the tag when present);
- streaming is unaffected: the incremental lexer buffers ambiguous tag prefixes, so a partially streamed `<arg_value>` never leaks into a value snapshot.

## Test Plan

- `tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py`: new non-streaming cases (single arg with missing opening tag; mixed malformed + well-formed args in one call) and a streaming case with the malformed sequence split across chunks; all pre-existing cases unchanged.
- Live validation on a 4×GPU GLM-5.2 deployment (`--tool-call-parser glm47`), replaying the production request that triggers the malformation at concurrency 6 with `logprobs: true`:
  - before: 12/120 responses parsed to `arguments: "{}"`;
  - after: 12/72 responses still show the raw malformation in sampled tokens (model-side quirk, expected), **all 12 parse to full arguments**, 0 empty; streaming replay 0/72 empty.

## Test Result

`pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py` — 16 passed.

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. The decode kernel (`TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS` / `KPOOL_HEAD`) and the AMD seed kernel already address the tail through `stride(0)` / `stride(1)`; only the NVIDIA seed kernel did not, and the existing regression test for exactly this layout was `skipif(not is_rocm)`.

**Why it shows up as "the cached system prompt is broken".** Only indexer blocks with id below `num_blocks * 2048 / 38016` (~5% of the pool) can be hit, and those are the ids handed out first after startup, i.e. the blocks of the first prefix-cached prompt, typically a long-lived system prompt. ## Summary

This PR adds a correctness-first CPU execution path for GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM5Next KDA for #57346.

The path is deliberately feature-local:

```text
GLM5Next common KDA layer
  -> CPU platform dispatch
  -> CPU state helpers and causal convolution
  -> CPU KDA recurrence/chunk contract
  -> optional _C_AVX512 recurrent operator
```

It does not implement #57345 (CPU sparse MLA / KeyPool), Kimi K3 support, a generic GDN refactor, or a new GLM CPU model hierarchy. The two GLM5Next CPU PRs are intentionally separate so that KDA and sparse MLA can be reviewed and tested independently.

### Scope and design

The initial source audit showed that CPU support required more than changing the two KDA imports. The common layer also reaches causal-convolution and state gather/scatter boundaries that have GPU-oriented implementations. I therefore kept the change at the GLM5Next KDA execution boundary and preserved the existing common projection, metadata, and routing code.

I did not add `glm5next/cpu/model.py` or a new backend registry. The hardware-specific difference is limited to KDA execution, so a model-level fork would add review and maintenance cost without solving a concrete blocker.

The related CPU GDN implementation was used as a reference for stateful CPU integration, but it was not treated as a drop-in KDA implementation. KDA differs in safe-gate semantics, beta handling, V-major state layout, and speculative state routing.

* q/k normalization and query scaling;

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA models keep a one-block-per-request circular tail cache (kpool). Every decode step — twice per step with MTP, once for the target model and once for the drafter — `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder.build()` maps each token to its request's tail ring with a chain of small torch ops (`arange` + `searchsorted` + `clamp` + `index_select` + `remainder` + `copy_`): 12 kernel launches and ~250 us of CPU enqueue time per build.

This PR replaces the chain with a single Triton kernel driven directly by `query_start_loc`, including the CUDA-graph padding rows. The CPU-tensor path keeps the torch implementation, and the emitted values are bit-identical to it.

With #57317 the generic `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` no longer runs for `KpoolTailSpec`, so `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` is now the only slot-mapping path for the tail group — this fusion covers all of it. It composes with #57477 (the seed-kernel stride fix): this PR only produces the logical slot ids (`block * kpool + pos % kpool`) that consumers decompose with `// kpool` / `% kpool`; physical addressing of the padded tail view is untouched, and the kernel reads the block table through its real `stride(0)`.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_qk_norm_rope` with `rotary_dim < head_dim` (partial rotary, e.g. GLM-4 / GLM-4.5 with `partial_rotary_factor=0.5`) only lets `rotary_lanes = rotary_dim / elems_per_lane` lanes into the RoPE branch. The neox path then calls `__shfl_xor_sync` / `__syncwarp` inside that branch with a full-warp mask, i.e. from a divergent branch where the mask names lanes that never arrive. That is undefined behaviour. With the single-head kernel it happens to produce the right values; with the N-token-heads kernel (`token_heads_per_warp > 1`, auto-selected on SM90 once `num_tokens * (num_heads + num_kv_heads) >= 10240`) it returns garbage or NaN on H200 for such layers.

## Changes

Do the warp exchange once before the lane guard with the whole warp participating; only the rotary lanes use the exchanged values. Same for both kernels. The `__syncwarp()` calls around the shuffle are no longer needed (the shuffle itself synchronises the participating lanes).

## Test plan

Standalone build of this file on H200 against a vLLM 0.28.0 install, compared with that install's `fused_qk_norm_rope`:

- full rotary (`rotary_dim == head_dim`) and all gptj/interleaved cases: bitwise identical to the shipped kernel before and after (bf16/fp16, head_dim 64/128/256, 1–8192 tokens, `token_heads_per_warp` 1/2/4/8).

This PR adds a correctness-first CPU sparse MLA / KeyPool execution path for GLM5Next for #57345.

The implementation keeps the common GLM5Next model graph and adds only the GLM-local CPU indexer, KeyPool lifecycle, metadata, and sparse MLA adapters required for execution. It is independent of the CPU KDA work in #57496.

### Why a GLM-specific path

The existing dense CPU MLA backend does not match the GLM5Next sparse contract. The DeepSeek CPU implementations were useful structural references, but GLM5Next has distinct KeyPool compression, gate-score pooling, pool-level top-k, pool-to-token expansion, incomplete-pool tails, index-cache representation, and request-local pool boundaries.

## Purpose

`DynamicVideoBackend` (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`, registered as `opencv_dynamic`)
sizes its frame-candidate walk directly from the request-supplied `fps`, so the
amount of work is unbounded by anything in the video:

```python
fps = target.fps
...
if duration <= max_duration:
    n = int(math.floor(duration * fps))
    frame_indices_list = sorted(
        {min(max_frame_idx, math.ceil(i / fps * original_fps)) for i in range(n)}
    )
```

`n` scales with `fps`, but the *result* does not: the largest index reachable is
`duration * original_fps` regardless, and the set deduplicates at the end. So a
large `fps` buys nothing and costs CPU linearly.

This applies the same clamp the sibling backends in this file already use —
`_MAX_FPS: ClassVar[int] = 30` plus `fps = min(target.fps, cls._MAX_FPS)`, which
is verbatim what `QwenVLVideoBackend` (`:362`/`:373`, from the merged #56729) and
`GLMGAVideoBackend` (`:812`/`:839`) do.

## Reachability

`fps` is request-controlled through `media_io_kwargs`, and nothing strips it for
this backend:

1. `opencv_dynamic` is registered with `video_processor="Glm4vVideoProcessor"`,
   so it is the **default** backend on GLM-4V-family servers — a plain
   `POST /v1/chat/completions` with
   `"media_io_kwargs": {"video": {"fps": 100000}}` is enough, no override needed.
2. It registers with the default `requires_gpu=False`, so
   `VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs` (`vllm/multimodal/media/video.py:60`) does **not**
   strip a request-level `video_backend: "opencv_dynamic"` either. The remaining
   `merge_kwargs` handling forwards `fps` verbatim.
3. It is also selected explicitly at
   `vllm/model_executor/models/nano_nemotron_vl.py:830`.

Only the `duration <= max_duration` branch is exposed. The `else` branch
self-bounds: `num_samples >= total_frames_num` short-circuits, and otherwise
`num_samples < total_frames_num`.
